**What the tests show**
- **Size of the changes:** 0.07–0.20% of pixels on 11 snapshots. Even magnified 8×, the baseline and current text look the same; only the anti-aliased edges of some letters are a fraction of a pixel off. `orders__phone` was flagged separately because its changes sit in one strip, but up close they're the same kind of edge difference.
- **Ruled out:**
  - The page structure, every element's size and position, and the computed styles all match the baselines exactly.
  - Every font, stylesheet and image loaded, and every character renders in the site's own font, with no fallback to another font.
  - The recorded environment (Chromium 153.0.8010.12, Ubuntu 24.04, viewport, scale) is the same as when the baselines were made.
  - The repo has a single commit and no uncommitted changes, so there's no earlier version to compare against or roll back to.
  - The CSS and JS use none of the text properties the style check skips.
  - Functional tests: 16/16 pass.
- **It's consistent:** two runs back to back produced identical screenshots. So it's not flakiness: this machine renders text very slightly differently from the one that made the baselines.

I rebuilt the font without that mapping in a scratch copy, and the differences tripled (0.3–0.8%). So the font had that mapping when the baselines were made and isn't the cause. **Most likely cause:** a text-rendering difference on the machine itself (for example a different CPU making the browser anti-alias text a bit differently), which the environment record doesn't capture. I can't confirm that from here.

- If you agree it's rendering noise, you can accept the new screenshots with `npx testivai approve --all` and commit `.testivai/baselines/`. I haven't done that, since it's your call.
